title: Host declaration
description: What the harness can do with subagents on one agent host (`hosts/<host>.json`). The host adapter must behave exactly as declared: an operation declared unsupported returns `unsupported_capability`, and one that answers anyway is refused as an invalid host result. Every claim carries where it came from, and a supported claim must rest on a source, never on an assumption.

host.description: The host name the hooks and adapters use; it must match the file name.

product.description: The product and surface every claim applies to.

verified_on.description: When the claims were last checked as a whole. Each claim also carries its own date.

subagents.description: Each subagent operation the harness can ask of this host.

notes.description: Prose that fits no field. Nothing reads it.

claim.description: Whether the harness can do this on the host, and why we believe it. Supported claims need a source; an unsupported one may be unsourced, which means nobody has shown it works, not that the host lacks it.

sourced.description: Ordered by strength: the vendor's documentation or code, then what this project observed on the host. A vendor claim quotes its source verbatim, because a paraphrase is where guessing comes back in.

source.description: The test, trial record, or command whose result shows it.

caveat.description: What is missing before this could be claimed.
